output.brief: What is going on: the rise is most likely not a clear change in real losses yet. Self-checkout cannot explain the Q2 rise, because the lanes were shut from 2 April to 26 June with failed payment terminals, and Q3 unscanned-item rates are at the chain median. Theft by the night stocker was checked on CCTV and found unsubstantiated. Store 14's rise is also not proven: interim figures are extrapolated from partial cycle counts with a wide margin of error, and about half of similar store rises were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Recorded shoplifting rose chain-wide after the new incident app launched in April, so the logs partly reflect reporting. Confidence is moderate; the 7 December full count is the real test. Next steps: keep store 14 in the December count, reject the proposal to drop it, hold off on store-specific guards, personnel action, or self-checkout removal until the count is compared with interim figures, and check whether the front-end and incident-reporting explanations hold. Please decide on the count by 20 November.
